package_info.package_versions: 0.19.6 (and likely 0.1.1, 0.1.0 for staging, but 0.19.6 is the first malicious version)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a build.rs script that collects host information (IP, country, region, platform) and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled Telegram channel during the build process. This behavior is not expected in legitimate Rust packages and constitutes a clear attempt to fingerprint and potentially target developers for further attacks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code collects host IP, country, region, and platform information using an external geolocation API, then sends this data to a hardcoded Telegram channel via the Telegram Bot API, enabling host fingerprinting and exfiltration of developer environment details.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code collects sensitive host information and exfiltrates it to an external service controlled by the attacker during the build process, which is not required for any legitimate build operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build.rs scripts are used for build-time configuration or code generation, not for collecting and exfiltrating host information over the network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate build.rs might check for platform or environment variables to configure compilation, but would never send this information to an external service.
key_indicators: Hardcoded Telegram bot token and channel ID
Network requests to external geolocation API (ip-api.com)
Network requests to api.telegram.org for data exfiltration
Creation of a mutex file to avoid repeated execution (anti-analysis/anti-forensics)
Collection of host-specific information (IP, country, region, platform)

attack_chain.action: During build, the build.rs script checks for a mutex file to avoid repeated execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: If not present, proceeds to collect host information.

attack_chain.action: The script collects host IP, country, region, and platform information using an external geolocation API.
attack_chain.leads_to: Prepares the collected data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The script formats the collected information and sends it to a hardcoded Telegram channel via the Telegram Bot API.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives host fingerprinting data, enabling further targeting or escalation.

behavioral_signatures: build.rs scripts making network requests during build-time
Exfiltration of host or environment information to external APIs (e.g., Telegram, Discord, webhook services)
Use of mutex files in OUT_DIR to avoid repeated execution (anti-analysis/anti-forensics)
Hardcoded tokens or channel IDs for messaging platforms
file_indicators: Presence of build.rs with network communication code
Mutex file creation in OUT_DIR during build
References to ip-api.com or api.telegram.org in build.rs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to api.telegram.org with /sendMessage endpoint
Unusual network activity during cargo build or package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build.rs scripts for network activity, especially requests to external APIs or messaging platforms. Flag any build.rs that contains hardcoded tokens, channel IDs, or references to known exfiltration endpoints (e.g., Telegram, Discord, webhook.site). Detect creation of mutex or marker files in OUT_DIR as a sign of anti-analysis behavior. Alert on any package that attempts to collect and transmit host or environment information during build or installation.
